title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: 1 in 3 Americans believe gambling is a better bet today than the stock market
body_text: By: Ray Day CONTACT: Ray Day ray.day@stagwellglobal.com We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from Stagwell and Allison Worldwide . Among the highlights of our weekly consumer sentiment tracking: STOCK MARKET HAS A REPUTATION PROBLEM The U.S. stock market is up 17.3% during the past 12 months. Yet you wouldn’t know that by the views of most Americans, according to our Harris Poll research with the Guardian . Two in five Americans believe the stock market only benefits the top 1%. A third believe they will have higher financial returns focusing more on gambling than the stock market. That increases to 46% among Millennials and to 44% among Gen Z. 65% of Americans wrongly believe that a growing stock market means the economy is growing. 38% don’t know the economy and stock market aren’t the same thing. Half of Americans believe today’s stock market is weak or are unsure how it is doing. AI’S MONEY ADVICE COMES WITH RISK Americans are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for personal finance help, yet the payoff is mixed, according to our Harris Poll research with NerdWallet. 26% of Americans say they’ve used an AI chatbot to answer personal finance questions. Among those users, 49% say they asked AI a money question in the past week. Americans are divided on trust, however: 45% say they trust AI chatbots to give good personal finance advice, while 55% do not. Among those using AI for finance questions, the top reasons are quick answers (50%) and avoiding multiple websites (35%). Oversharing is a concern: 77% of users shared some kind of personal information with a chatbot, including 38% who shared their credit score, 9% who shared their Social Security number and 10% who shared account numbers. See also: 81% of Americans Would Let an AI Agent Handle Part of Their Job Search BUY NOW, PAY LATER Americans see Buy Now, Pay Later plans as a smart, flexible alternative to high-interest credit cards, according to research from HarrisX and the Financial Technology Association. 77% of U.S. adults say BNPL plans have had a net positive impact on American consumers, rising to 91% among users. 74% say BNPL is better for their financial well-being than high-interest credit cards. 78% say they would recommend BNPL to a friend or family member, while 7% would not. The top reasons users choose BNPL are to spread out costs without interest (89%), gain greater flexibility (88%) and have more control over payments (86%). Among all U.S. adults, roughly three-quarters agree BNPL helps consumers budget (76%), avoid high-interest credit card debt (76%) and navigate financial hardship (75%). A BOOM AT THE BOX OFFICE Going to the movies is back in America, according to the State of Cinema Report from Stagwell’s The People Platform . People are attracted to a wider variety of films than in recent years – with nearly 390 million movie admissions recorded in the first half of 2026. That’s one of the strongest moviegoing environments since the pandemic. The Top 10 films accounted for 57% of total admissions. The next tier also mattered – titles ranked 11–20 delivered another 22%, showing the box office rebound is being powered by depth. Family titles still led the market, with The Super Mario Galaxy Movie (11%) and Toy Story 5 (9%) combining for 20% of admissions. PG and PG-13 titles make up seven of the year’s Top 10 films, yet R-rated films are also pulling real weight, making up 30.5% of total admissions and reinforcing that audiences are engaging across ratings and genres. Nearly half of all moviegoers are adults 18–34, including 25% women and 21% men 18–34. ICYMI: In case you missed it, check out the thought-leadership and happenings around Stagwell making news: Which Sports Should You Sponsor in 2028? title: Archives Of Nethys Loses Paizo Support, DnD Encounters Goes To Thay, Roll20 Works With UVTT – TTRPG News 7/17/2026
summary: Paizo pulls official licensing for Archives of Nethys, WotC gives dates for the next DnD Encounters season, and Roll20 now supports maps with built-in dynamic lighting.
body_text: Big news this week in the world of tabletop RPGs! Today’s headlines are short, but the details go deep. Fortunately for you, we’ve summarized the important bits here and provided the necessary links should you want to read further. This week: Paizo pulls official licensing for Archives of Nethys, WotC gives dates for the next DnD Encounters season, and Roll20 now supports maps with built-in dynamic lighting. Paizo Ends Licensing Contract With Archives Of Nethys Players of Paizo RPGs were in for some bad news this week as the publisher announced the end of its licensing relationship with website Archives of Nethys . The website contains all rules for Pathfinder and Starfinder for free, often a selling point when fans try to recruit new players. New content was put on the site as soon as books launched, and official artwork was displayed. However, with the agreement no longer in place, the official artwork must be taken down. All rules will still stay up for free , but the Archives team announced that they’ll no longer get early access to books for posting rules on release day. They now need to buy the books and add them to the site over time. The decision seems to be an effect of Paizo’s recent money troubles due to the Diamond distribution bankruptcy . DnD Encounters Season Of Magic Details Revealed via: WotC Wizards of the Coast put out the schedule for its next DnD organized play event, Season of Magic . The short storyline takes players from levels 3-5 as they combat the Red Wizards of Thay , running parallel to the events of Arcana Unleashed: Deadfall. Celebration kickoff events begin the season as early as September 4 but can happen anytime that month. Then, weekly play sessions happen through late September and through October. According to ICv2 , players get a promo d20 for participating. Roll20 Now Supports UVTT Files via Roll20 Roll20 Game Masters can now upload maps in the UVTT format and instantly benefit from their dynamic lighting presets. The platform announced the update this week as part of its new Create Page menu. The new drop-down menu for pages gives options for creating a blank page like before, drawing a map in real time with Dungeon Scrawl , randomly generating a dungeon , and uploading an image file directly to Map Layer. With this new framework for uploading, Roll20 now supports UVTT files in all their glory without need for mods. Free users will not be able to benefit from dynamic lighting as that feature is reserved for paid tiers. But should they decide to go for a paid subscription, their maps will automatically update to provide the preset lighting features. ‍ Few stories this week but very impactful ones! Thanks for reading, have fun this weekend, and may your dice be kind. Sergio Solórzano is the best Dungeon Master in the USA (according to an official D&D competition , anyway). He loves minis and terrain but also goes all-in on improv! title: How to Start an LLC in California: A Comprehensive Guide
summary: Wondering how to start an LLC in California? Find out everything you need to know about forming an LLC, from tax requirements to business licenses.
body_text: An operating agreement outlining the ownership structure, management rules, and other vital company information is a key document for your LLC. Creating a comprehensive plan can help prevent future disputes and maintain smooth operations within your LLC. The document must adhere to the California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act's requirements, ensuring that the rights and responsibilities of LLC owners are clearly defined. To draft your LLC operating agreement, consider using a California LLC operating agreement template as a starting point. Customizing the template to suit your business's specific needs will ensure that your agreement accurately reflects your LLC's structure and goals. With a well-crafted operating agreement in place, your LLC will have a solid foundation for growth and success. Step 5: Get an employer identification number (EIN) Any California LLC fundamentally requires an employer identification number (EIN) , also known as a Federal Tax Identification Number. It is an essential tool to validate your LLC and start working on business operations. This unique number, issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), allows you to handle tax filings, open a business bank account and business credit card, and hire employees. Applying for an EIN is a straightforward process, with the IRS offering a free online application. Even if your California LLC is a single-member entity with no employees, obtaining an EIN can still be beneficial. Using an EIN instead of your personal Social Security number for business purposes can help protect against identity theft. With an EIN in hand, you'll be prepared to manage your LLC's finances and comply with tax requirements. Step 6: Comply with California licenses and permits The next step in figuring out how to form an LLC in California involves obtaining the appropriate business licenses and permits. To operate your California LLC legally, you must fulfill federal, state, and local government regulations. This includes obtaining necessary health permits, building permits, and signage permits, among other requirements. Adherence to these regulations ensures the smooth operation of your LLC and helps to avoid potential legal issues. Information about business licenses can be found at your local county clerk's office or the Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development's website, CalGold. Step 7: Maintain good standing with the California Secretary of State For the continued success of your LLC, it's important to maintain good standing with the California Secretary of State and the California Franchise Tax Board. This involves filing required documents, such as the Statement of Information, and paying annual franchise taxes and other fees to the California Franchise Tax Board. The Statement of Information contains supplemental contact information and details regarding your company's finances and must be filed within 90 days of formation. You must submit an updated Statement of Information with the California Secretary of State every two years and pay the $20 filing fee. Prompt submission of necessary documents and payment of fees ensures that your California LLC continues to maintain good standing with the Secretary of State. This will help you avoid potential penalties and maintain a positive reputation for your business.

title: Vertiv Extends Newest Rackmount UPS Line to Support Larger Edge Deployments in North America
summary: Vertiv announced the addition of new models of the Vertiv™ Liebert® GXT5 family of rackmount, on-line uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems. The new capacities extend the Liebert GXT5 product ratings with 10 models between 3000VA and 10kVA for higher voltage deployments.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio [Sept. 12, 2019] – Vertiv today announced the addition of new models of the Vertiv™ Liebert® GXT5 family of rackmount, on-line uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems. The new capacities extend the Liebert GXT5 product ratings with 10 models between 3000VA and 10kVA for higher voltage deployments. The new models are available in 208V only, and refreshed models supporting 208V/120V configurations through Vertiv partners in North America. Vertiv introduced the Liebert GXT5 in June, updating the 500VA to 3000VA, 120V models of the popular rackmount UPS system. The Liebert GXT5 has a power factor of up to 1.0 on the 5000VA to 10kVA models and is more efficient in both on-line (up to 95 percent) and Active ECO mode (up to 98 percent) than previous models. All Liebert GXT5 models are ENERGY STAR 2.0 certified, and RoHS and REACH compliant. “The Liebert GXT5 is designed for today’s increasingly critical small IT environments and edge locations, and that includes higher capacity edge sites that demand low latency and high availability to deliver the advanced applications and services today’s users expect,” said Ramesh Menon, vice president of small UPS at Vertiv. The Liebert GXT5 is the latest addition to the Vertiv channel product portfolio in North America and seamlessly integrates with other products in the portfolio to support single-rack or more complex edge deployments. The Liebert GXT5 offers scalable runtime options, with additional external battery cabinets that ensure availability even during extended interruptions. It can be managed remotely and has integrated maintenance bypass and flexible output receptacle configurations to meet the connected equipment requirements of any site. When used together with the free Trellis™ Power Insight , users can monitor and manage up to 100 supported Vertiv devices. Along with the highest level of equipment protection available in a rack configuration, the Liebert® GXT5 offers a three-year full coverage factory warranty for the UPS and battery, a leading warranty in the industry. The system also is available with the Vertiv™ Power Assurance Package, which delivers convenient and cost-effective support for power delivery to small IT sites, and other service packages, to support individual customer needs. For more information on the Liebert GXT5 UPS, Vertiv and the Vertiv channel program, visit Vertiv.com . About Vertiv Vertiv brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to ensure its customers’ vital applications run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, USA, Vertiv employs around 20,000 people and does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, and for the latest news and content from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . CONTACT Vince McMorrow T +614 383 1622 E Vince.McMorrow@Fahlgren.com

title: Competing off the field: How college athletic departments can win with AI-powered communications
summary: College athletic departments now run NIL compliance, donor relations, and international recruiting through communication systems that were never built for
body_text: College athletic departments now run NIL compliance, donor relations, and international recruiting through communication systems that were never built for it. AI-powered communications can close that gap, answering every call, tracking every conversation, and giving compliance teams a searchable record automatically. Here’s what that looks like in practice: When a prospective recruit’s family calls an athletic department, they are not just asking about scholarships and practice schedules. They are forming an impression of the institution. If that call goes to voicemail, takes too long to route to the right person, or gets answered inconsistently depending on who picks up – that impression sticks. College athletic departments have become some of the most complex operations on any campus. Institutions must manage NIL (Name, Image, Likeness) agreements and ensure compliance oversight that influences nearly every interaction a department has with athletes, agents, donors, and collectives. Simultaneously, many departments face the challenge of accomplishing more with stagnant or reduced budgets while competing with peer institutions that are heavily investing in enhancing the student-athlete experience. The cost of a missed call, a miscommunicated NIL disclosure, or a slow response to a recruit has never been higher. And for most athletic departments, the communication systems in place were not built for the moment they are now in. A department under pressure from every direction The communication challenges facing athletic departments today are not isolated – they compound. Compliance offices are tracking verbal commitments, text confirmations, and phone conversations that now function as potential audit items under the new oversight regime. Ticketing and donor relations teams are fielding questions from fans and major donors who expect the same responsiveness they receive from consumer brands. Recruiting coordinators are trying to make first impressions on international student-athletes and their families, often in languages that their current staff cannot support at scale. Meanwhile, the operational baseline has eroded. Every unanswered call or slow reply is potential revenue walking away. A recruit who feels unheard, a donor who doesn’t get a callback, a fan who can’t resolve a ticketing question—the cost adds up fast. For a ticketing office missing a season-ticket renewal call, that is direct revenue lost. For a recruiting office missing a family’s inquiry during an official visit window, it may be a scholarship offer that never gets made. Staff burnout compounds the problem. The transfer portal and compressed recruiting cycles have made athlete movement constant, while support and operations staff report rising workloads from repetitive inquiries, after-hours demand, and manual administrative tasks. Departments face a paradox: the moment they need their best people focused on high-impact relationships, those people are buried in routine call handling. A smarter approach to athletic department communications Meeting the demands of the modern athletic department requires more than a phone system upgrade. It requires a communication infrastructure that automates the routine, supports staff in real time, and turns every interaction into institutional knowledge – while creating the documented, auditable record that NIL and revenue-sharing compliance now demands. RingCentral’s AI-powered platform unifies phone, SMS, team messaging, and video for staff (RingEX), adds a full omnichannel contact center for high-volume constituent engagement (RingCX), and embeds agentic voice AI across every interaction. The result is a single, secure front door for the entire department, one that scales to game-day surges, covers recruiting inquiries after hours, and never lets a conversation disappear into a personal cell phone. How does AI Receptionist (AIR) handle recruiting calls after hours? AI Receptionist (AIR) serves as an always-on virtual receptionist for every team, office, and function within the department. Whether it is a recruit calling the football office at 9:00 p.m., a donor trying to reach the development team during a bowl week, or a fan asking about parking and will-call on a Saturday morning, AIR answers every call and text 24/7 with a natural, human-like tone, no rigid phone menus, no voicemail black holes. Departments can run distinct AIR instances for ticketing, compliance, development, and individual sports, giving every team a tailored front door. For international recruits and their families, AIR detects and switches languages mid-conversation automatically, removing one of the most common friction points in global recruiting. How does AI Virtual Assistant (AVA) support staff during NIL and eligibility conversations? AI Virtual Assistant (AVA) supports staff during every interaction – drafting and translating messages, summarizing meetings, and capturing key decisions and follow-up actions automatically. For compliance officers and operations coordinators managing back-to-back conversations about NIL arrangements and eligibility questions, AVA removes the administrative weight of manual note-taking and keeps attention on the athlete, not the paperwork. How does AI Conversation Expert (ACE) support NIL disclosure documentation? AI Conversation Expert (ACE) analyzes 100% of conversations across voice, chat, and meetings, generating summaries, transcripts, and quality evaluations automatically. For compliance and revenue-sharing teams, ACE provides a complete, searchable audit trail of what was communicated and when, the documented backbone that the new College Sports Commission oversight and NIL disclosure requirements demand. At the program level, ACE surfaces patterns across interactions: what recruits ask most, where donors hesitate, which FAQs are generating the highest call volume – giving leadership the evidence base to make smarter staffing, messaging, and investment decisions. What platform do athletic department staff use to coordinate across teams? RingEX gives athletic department staff—from coaching staff to compliance officers to ticketing coordinators—a single platform for phone, SMS, team messaging, and video. Cross-functional coordination that currently lives across personal cell phones, shared inboxes, and disconnected scheduling tools moves into one unified system with complete visibility and a consistent audit trail. What AI-powered communications looks like inside an athletic department Here is how these capabilities come together during a critical window in the recruiting calendar: A highly recruited prospect and their family are on campus for an official visit. While the coaching staff is running the on-field portion of the day, the family has questions – about the academic support program, about financial aid timelines, about how the NIL program works. They call the main athletic department number. AIR answers immediately, understands their questions in natural language, provides accurate answers drawn from the department’s own documentation, and routes the family to a senior recruiting coordinator with a full summary of what was asked and answered. The family never has to repeat themselves. The coordinator walks in prepared. That evening, a major donor calls the development office after hours to ask about their suite renewal and whether the naming rights conversation from last month’s lunch is moving forward. AIR handles the suite renewal inquiry completely and leaves a detailed message for the development officer, including a summary of the naming rights question – to review first thing in the morning. Nothing falls through the cracks. The following week, the compliance office is reviewing its NIL disclosure documentation ahead of a College Sports Commission inquiry. ACE has automatically captured and organized summaries of every relevant conversation—calls with the athlete’s agent, texts with the collective, internal review discussions—into a searchable, timestamped record. What would have taken a compliance officer hours of manual review is ready in minutes. Across the department, staff who once spent hours on repetitive call handling are redirected to the work that requires human judgment: building relationships with recruits, stewarding major donors, and supporting student-athletes through the challenges of balancing competition, academics, and personal-brand obligations. Building a communication infrastructure for the new era of college athletics College athletics has entered a period of profound structural change. Revenue sharing, NIL oversight, a compressed transfer portal, international recruiting, and rising constituent expectations have arrived simultaneously – on top of budgets that are not growing fast enough to match the demand. Departments that try to manage this complexity with legacy phone systems, disconnected tools, and stretched staff are accepting a competitive disadvantage. An always-on AI receptionist that answers every call in the caller’s language, a unified staff platform that keeps coordination visible and documented, and conversation intelligence that turns every interaction into institutional insight, together, these give athletic departments the communication infrastructure the moment requires. Winning recruiting battles, deepening donor relationships, and navigating NIL compliance all come down to one thing: how fast and how consistently a department communicates at every touchpoint. RingCentral makes that possible. title: What is the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)?
summary: What is the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)? Cyber Resilience Act What is the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)? The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is a European Union regulation that establishes mandatory cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements, including hardware, software, and connected devices. The CRA aims to ensure products are secure by design, supported throughout their lifecycle, and better protected against evolving cyber threats. Why CRA Matters The growing number of connected products has increased the need for stronger cybersecurity protections. The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) helps address this challenge by establishing common cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements placed on the EU market. The regulation improves transparency, strengthens product security throughout the lifecycle, and helps organizations and consumers make more informed technology decisions.
